title: Appointed by Thee, We Meet in Thy Name
description: Appointed by Thee, We Meet in Thy Name in Tonic Solfa to LYONS, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 484.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in 10.10.11.11, and this page sets them to LYONS; any other 10.10.11.11 tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ap-point-ed by thee, We meet in thy name, And meek-ly a-gree To fol_-low the Lamb, To trace thy e-xam-ple, The world to dis-dain, And con-stant-ly tram-ple On plea_-sure and pain.

lines: Appointed by thee, We meet in thy name,
And meekly agree To follow the Lamb,
To trace thy example, The world to disdain,
And constantly trample On pleasure and pain.
Rejoicing, in hope, we humbly go on,
And daily take up The pledge of our crown;
In doing and bearing The will of our Lord,
We still are preparing To meet our reward.
O Jesus, appear! No longer delay
To sanctify here, And bear us away,
The end of our meeting On earth let us see,
Triumphantly sitting In glory with thee!

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to LYONS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
